title: Fourier coefficient under product noise
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by $\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For $\rho\in[0,1]$, let the product noise operator independently retain each input coordinate with probability $\rho$ and otherwise resample it from $\pi$. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ and a multi-index $a\in\iota^n$, the Fourier coefficient of the noisy function at $a$ is $\rho^d$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $a$, where $d$ is the number of coordinates where $a$ differs from the constant index.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
The basis is indexed by $\iota$ and spans the real-valued functions on $\Omega$
The basis vector at the distinguished index is constant $1$
